 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the MV Act, challenging the impugned judgment and award dated 18.12.2017 passed in MVC No.3432/2012 by the learned XXII Additional Court of Small Causes and Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, Bangalore (SCCH-24).

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act claiming just and proper compensation for the death of H.S. Raju who succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

The Tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.9,89,594/- with interest at 8% p.a.
3.
The appellant-BMTC is in appeal challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribuna as well as the liability.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text:
2 5. The Tribunal while attributing contributory negligence against the rider of the motor cycle in which the deceased was traveling has observed as follows:
"Admittedly, all the 3 persons were major at the time of accident.

Furthermore, the Sketch produced at Ex.P.4 in MVC.3383/2012 and MVC.7769/2012 clearly depicts that in a vide 'U' turn, both the driver of the BMTC bus who was coming in Bengaluru-Tumakuru Highway was entering into service road and the rider of the motor cycle along with 2 pillion riders was going to enter Bengaluru-Tumakuru Highway from the service road, were taking turns on extreme edge of the median which had put between NH-4 and service road towards Tumakuru near Raghavendra U turn.
Hence, both the vehicles collided with each other and resulted in the unfortunate incident.

Looking to the above said oral evidence of petitioners and eye-witness as well as the sketch, I came to conclusion that apart from the lack of negligence on the part of the driver of the offending BMTC Bus, the said 3 persons who were traveling in the motorcycle have also contravened the traffic rules and contributed some part of negligence in occurrence of the accident.

29. The learned counsel for the petitioners MVC.4469/2012 have relied on the decisions reported in:
1) 2011(4) AIR KAR 91, between Divisional Controller, KSRTC, Urban Division,
Mysore V/s Mahadevamma and others.
Wherein it is held that, "Motor Vehicles Act (59 of 1988), Ss.168, 147- Rash and negligent driving - Third party risk -
Evidence shows that bus moved on its right side and had space it left -

Despite that it NC:
2024:KHC:21445 moved on right side and caused accident - Accident could have been avoided by driver of bus if he had taken little care-

Mere fact that deceased were three persons on motor bike and same was in violation of permit-It cannot be said that they were negligent-Evidence shows that driver of bus was negligent in driving-Since deceased were third parties -Entitled to compensation".
2) 2013 ACJ 2008, between Narmada Prasad Choure and others V/s Nanakram Pavar and others wherein it is held that, "Negligence - Contributory negligence - Pillion rider - Whether traveling as a pillion rider on motorcycle carrying more than two pillion riders tantamounts to contributory negligence on the part of the pillion rider - Held on."

entities.text: Narmada Prasad Choure and others V/s Nanakram Pavar and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have gone through the decisions supra; The principle laid down in the decisions is aptly applicable to the present case on hand to certain extent.

Under these circumstances, the evidence of P.W.1 in MVC.3432/12 and MVC.7769/2012 and PW.2 in MVC.3383/2012 and PW.3 in all the cases coupled with documents produced through PW.1 and 2, sufficiently establishes that the accident has occurred due to the gross negligent driving of the BMTC Bus by its driver and some contributory negligence on the part of the rider and pillion riders of MotorCycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-AX-7821 and the petitioner Ravikumar has sustained grievous injuries and Raju. H.S and Ramesh of MVC.
3432/2012 and MVC.7769/2012, did not recover and succumbed to the said ) accidental injuries.
Bangalore Metropolitan Transport ... vs Sri Shekarappa on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159726486/
3 6.

The Tribunal has attributed contributory negligence to the extent of 20% to the rider of the motorcycle and 80% to the NC: 2024:KHC:21445 driver of the bus belonging to the Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC).
Upon appreciating the evidence on record and finding no perversity or arbitrariness, I do not find any illegality in the Tribunal's findings.
7. At the time of the accident, the deceased was 24 years old.
The Tribunal assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.5,500/- per month based on Exhibit P.16, the salary certificate.

After adding 40%
towards the loss of future income, the Tribunal rightly awarded compensation for the loss of dependency.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.
However, the interest awarded at the rate of 8% per annum requires reduction.

8. The claimants are entitled to a compensation amount of Rs.7,91,675/-, which shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the petition until actual realization, as opposed to the 8% per annum awarded by the Tribunal.
To this extent, the impugned award is modified.
The statutory amount in deposit is to be transmitted to the Jurisdictional Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appeal is disposed of.
